meta.edition: SF Rent Increase Compliance & Verification Suite (/compliance/)
meta.neighborhood: Outer Sunset · San Francisco, CA 94122 · Reported 1940 Two-Unit Building
meta.privacy_statement: Zero personal tenant names, initials, street addresses, APN/parcel identifiers, email addresses, or private phone numbers appear anywhere in this dashboard or its underlying JSON. Tenants are referenced exclusively via synthetic placeholders (Placeholder Tenant 1A–1D and Placeholder Tenant 2A–2B); dates and dollar figures from the owner brief are preserved strictly as unverified scenario inputs.
meta.legal_disclaimer: Educational and compliance verification resource grounded in primary .gov authorities live-fetched on 2026-11-10. Not legal advice and not a certification to serve notice until all flagged private lease, ledger, license, coverage, and habitability facts are verified.

case_inputs.item: Year built & Certificate of Occupancy (reported 1940 two-unit building in 94122)
case_inputs.impact: Pre-June 14, 1979 multi-unit residential buildings are presumptively subject to SF Rent Ordinance rent control and eviction protections unless a specific parcel exemption applies.

case_inputs.item: Unit 1 active SF Rent Board Housing Inventory submission & Rent Increase License
case_inputs.impact: Hard statutory gate under §37.15(e): without an active license on the increase effective date, any annual or banked increase is suspended and permanently uncollectible for suspension months.

case_inputs.item: Unit 2 active SF Rent Board Housing Inventory submission & Rent Increase License
case_inputs.impact: Each tenant-occupied dwelling unit requires its own Housing Inventory submission and active Rent Increase License on portal.sfrb.org before an increase takes effect.

case_inputs.item: Owner's non-rental SF business activity, payroll expense, or short-term rental status (Business Registration Certificate check)
case_inputs.impact: One residential structure with <4 units does not by itself require a Treasurer Business Registration Certificate, but other SF business activity, payroll expense, or short-term rentals trigger registration.

case_inputs.item: Unit 1 April 1, 2026 tenancy agreement type (fixed-term renewal vs. month-to-month / addendum)
case_inputs.brief_input: Continuing tenancy April 1, 2026 @ $3,995.00/mo (Placeholder Tenant 1A + Placeholder Tenant 1D)
case_inputs.impact: Under California law, rent cannot be increased during a fixed-term lease unless the written lease expressly authorizes mid-term increases.

case_inputs.item: Unit 1 verified current base rent excluding temporary passthroughs, plus full ledger since Feb. 1, 2025
case_inputs.brief_input: Initial lease Feb. 1, 2025 @ $3,995.00/mo (Placeholder Tenants 1A, 1B, 1C); continuing Apr. 1, 2026 @ $3,995.00/mo
case_inputs.impact: Determines exact base rent, anniversary date, and whether the 1.4% 2025–26 allowance is eligible for banking on February 1, 2027.

case_inputs.item: Whether a timely written Rule 6.14 notice was served on Placeholder Tenant 1D within 60 days of actual knowledge (~May 31, 2026)
case_inputs.impact: Does NOT allow a market reset today because original Placeholder Tenant 1A still resides there, but governs whether a §6.14 reset could apply in the future if Tenant 1A vacates.

case_inputs.item: Legal status of Placeholder Tenant 1D (co-tenant with direct landlord agreement/rent acceptance vs. subtenant)
case_inputs.brief_input: Listed alongside Placeholder Tenant 1A on April 1, 2026
case_inputs.impact: Under Costa-Hawkins §1954.53(d), a co-tenant who moved in after the original occupant is NOT subject to a Costa-Hawkins market reset even if the last original occupant later leaves.

case_inputs.item: Unit 2 verified current base rent and complete 2019–2026 rent/passthrough ledger
case_inputs.brief_input: Last lease start June 1, 2019 @ $3,150.00/mo (Placeholder Tenant 2A & Placeholder Tenant 2B)
case_inputs.impact: Critical gate: $3,150.00 was supplied only as the June 1, 2019 lease-start rent. Any intervening rent increase between 2019 and 2026 changes both current base rent and banked percentages.

case_inputs.item: Open DBI/DPH Notices of Violation (>35 days unabated) or unresolved tenant repair requests in Unit 1 or Unit 2
case_inputs.impact: Cal. Civ. Code §1942.4 bars issuing a rent increase notice if a citation is >35 days unabated; SF Form 516B lets tenants defer an annual increase within 60 days if requested repairs remain unmade.

case_inputs.item: Protected habitability complaints, agency inspections, or tenant-rights activity within the preceding 180 days
case_inputs.impact: Cal. Civ. Code §1942.5 bars retaliatory rent increases within 180 days of protected tenantability complaints and at any time when motivated by retaliation.

case_inputs.item: Presence of Housing Choice Voucher (Section 8), HOPWA, or government regulatory rent agreement on either unit
case_inputs.impact: Subsidized tenancies follow SF Admin. Code §37.3(a)(10) Payment Standard / Housing Authority rules and FEHA source-of-income protections.

case_inputs.item: Whether any notice mailed under CCP §1013(a) is mailed and addressed wholly within California
case_inputs.brief_input: Property in SF 94122; owner/tenant mailing locations unverified
case_inputs.impact: CCP §1013(a) adds +5 calendar days within California, +10 calendar days if mailed/addressed outside California within the U.S., and +20 calendar days outside the U.S.

case_inputs.item: Official government 'normal' or market rent-increase rate specific to Outer Sunset ZIP 94122
case_inputs.impact: No official .gov agency publishes a ZIP-94122 market rent-increase benchmark; left blank rather than substituting commercial listing blogs.

case_inputs.item: SF Rent Board allowable annual rent-increase percentage for March 1, 2027 – February 29, 2028
case_inputs.brief_input: Effective dates on or after March 1, 2027
case_inputs.impact: Not yet published by the SF Rent Board as of 2026-11-10; any notice taking effect on or after March 1, 2027 must use the 2027–28 Form 571 rate once published.

case_inputs.item: Official SF Rent Board dataset comparing annual/banking behavior of corporate vs. individual landlords
case_inputs.brief_input: Corporate vs. individual landlord comparison inquiry
case_inputs.impact: No official SF .gov publication tabulates rent-increase frequency by owner entity type; left blank to avoid unsupported generalizations.

scenarios.label: Routine Annual-Only (2026–27 Allowance)
scenarios.gate_summary: Requires month-to-month status or lease escalation clause (CF-05), active license on effective date (CF-02), verified base rent (CF-06), and clean repair/retaliation record.

scenarios.label: Conditional Annual + 1 Skipped Year Banked (on Feb 1, 2027)
scenarios.pending_261020_exposure: None (1.4% banked is well below 10.0% proposed cap)
scenarios.gate_summary: Satisfies both 24-month no-increase (SF.gov) and 12-month post-eligibility (Rule 4.12(a)) tests on 2027-02-01 ONLY if Feb 1, 2025 tenancy had zero intervening increases and Apr 1, 2026 did not lock a fixed term.

scenarios.label: Routine Annual-Only (Lowest-Friction / Zero Pending-Bill Exposure)
scenarios.pending_261020_exposure: None (0.0% banked; any verified unused allowances stay banked)
scenarios.gate_summary: Requires verifying $3,150.00 is current base rent (CF-09), active Unit 2 license (CF-03), and clean repair/retaliation record.

scenarios.label: Enacted-Law Full Conditional Catch-Up (6 Skipped Years + Current Annual)
scenarios.pending_261020_exposure: HIGH WATCH: 11.5% banked exceeds File #261020's proposed 10.0% banked cap (for notices >= Sept 15, 2026) by 1.5% if enacted as drafted
scenarios.gate_summary: Assumes zero rent increases since June 1, 2019 (unverified CF-09). Triggers 90-day personal / 95-day CA mail notice under Civ. Code §827(b)(3). Check Legistar File #261020 before serving.

scenarios.label: File #261020 Risk-Mitigated Partial Banked Catch-Up (10.0% Banked + 1.6% Annual)
scenarios.pending_261020_exposure: Mitigated under current draft Digest (banked portion capped at exactly 10.0%; remaining 1.5% stays banked)
scenarios.gate_summary: Uses Topic 503 partial-banking rule so banked portion <=10.0% while total 11.6% still requires 90-day personal / 95-day CA mail notice. Still requires verified 2019–2026 ledger (CF-09).
